(CNN)Madonna has a thing for making out with fellow performers on stage.
First it was Britney and Christina, and now rapper Drake has been on the receiving end of a little lip action from Madge.
While the blondes had fun with it, Drake appeared less than enthused after Madonna's prolonged smooch onstage at the Coachella music festival in California on Sunday.
In an update Monday from "champagnepapi" himself on Instagram, the rapper clarified his reaction: "Don't misinterpret my shock!!
I got to make out with the queen Madonna and I feel 100 about that forever.
Thank you @Madonna."
After the kiss, though, he seemed dazed.
"Oh, s***.
What the f*** just happened?"
he asked moments later from the stage.
It all went down after Drake performed  "Madonna," a song named for the megastar off his new mixtape "If You're Reading This It's Too Late," according to Billboard.
He welcomed Madonna onstage as a special guest to perform a few songs.
While wrapping up "Human Nature," the Material Girl, 56, planted one on the seated Drake, 28, who began to flail his arms after a while in an apparent attempt to escape.
His sour face after the encounter led many to speculate that he didn't enjoy the kiss.
Of course, Drake and Madonna's little makeout sesh got the web talking and meme-ing: .
"So @Drake proves that kissing @Madonna is about as ghastly as I always imagined it would be," wrote former CNN personality Piers Morgan.
"Grandma: give Nana some suga .
Drake: no no noooooo!!!"
wrote another Tweeter.

You summarize English text according to the requested conditions while staying grounded in the source.

Summarize the source text below in English according to these instructions.

## Conditions for this summary
These are the conditions for this summary.
- Length: Keep it very short: two sentences or fewer.
- Use of source wording: Select complete sentences verbatim from the source. Do not change words or punctuation or write new sentences. Only whitespace normalization and omission of a leading document publisher tag (CNN) or (The Hollywood Reporter), case-insensitively, are allowed. Do not remove attribution inside a sentence.

## Preserve source facts and central information
- Source fidelity takes priority over stylistic preferences. Never change a fact or invent a connection or cause to meet a length or wording condition.
- Before drafting, identify the central subject and event, main outcome or intended goal, decisive amounts with units and time windows, and essential qualifications or uncertainty within the requested focus.
- Preserve who made each claim. Keep allegations, plans, estimates and unknowns distinct from confirmed facts. Copy numbers, dates and names accurately.
- Within the requested sentence count, choose wording or source sentences that preserve the most central information. Remove decorative openings, peripheral background and repetition first.
- For verbatim extraction, choose source sentences carrying central information. If a pronoun or event link would be unclear, include its necessary context within the sentence limit or choose a clearer sentence. Do not invent connecting text.
- If everything cannot fit, retain the most important source-supported information within the requested length and wording mode. Do not silently exceed the length or claim complete coverage.
- Before submitting, compare the summary with the source for missing central events, outcomes or goals, decisive quantities and qualifications, added facts, and altered attribution. Do not output this check.

## Output format
Output only the summary, in English. No preamble, title, checklist, explanation, or closing.

supplement: Read through the whole source before selecting material; the opening event can supply context while later passages carry the article's distinctive focus. Give sentence space to distinct central developments or perspectives, rather than repeated setup, vivid scene-setting, or several details about the same event. A prominent response or conclusion can be central even when it contains no numerical result. For strict extraction, consider candidate sentence combinations as a whole: prefer those that jointly retain the main event and another central aspect with clear referents and intact attribution. Do not automatically copy an opening sentence merely to introduce a name. Keep context necessary to understand selected sentences; when that context would consume the available budget, choose a clearer combination. When rewriting is permitted, combine compatible source clauses only when their subjects, status, and attribution remain clear. Use additional permitted space to preserve substantive distinctions, not repetition. Apply all base constraints throughout; do not lengthen a short extractive summary or alter copied sentences to force in every point.
